# A target whose depth the empty-level drop and the fold both touch

A cross-reference target has three level counts once both rules have run: the
levels the author wrote, the levels left after an empty one is dropped, and the
three the LaTeX back-end stores. The report about the fold names the second, so
it names the first alongside it whenever they differ — a number the author
cannot find in the value they typed is a number they cannot act on.

The entry every target below points at, written four levels deep and printed as
three: [larch]{.index entry="Larch!Maple!Nutmeg!Olive"}.

A `see=` target written with five levels whose first is empty. Four survive the
drop, which is one more than the ceiling, so the fold rewrites it and the report
names four against the five written: [teak]{.index entry="Teak"
see="!Larch!Maple!Nutmeg!Olive"}.

The same shape with the empty level at the other end. makeindex treats the two
ends in opposite ways, so neither is evidence about the other, and the count a
report names must come out the same either way:
[willow]{.index entry="Willow" see="Larch!Maple!Nutmeg!Olive!"}.

The same shape again on `see-also=`, so the report is known to name both counts
whichever attribute carries the target: [yewtree]{.index entry="Yewtree"
see-also="!Larch!Maple!Nutmeg!Olive"}.

# The two shapes that must read differently

A target written with four levels, none of them empty. The fold rewrites it
exactly as it rewrites the ones above, but nothing was dropped, so there is no
second number to give and the report names four alone. This is the control that
tells a report giving both counts where they differ from one that always gives
two: [zircon]{.index entry="Zircon" see="Larch!Maple!Nutmeg!Olive"}.

A target written with four levels whose first is empty, pointing at an entry
three levels deep. Three survive the drop, which is exactly the ceiling, so
nothing is folded and the fold report must not fire at all — the counts differ
here, and a report that fired on that alone would tell an author their target
was rewritten when it was not. The empty level itself is still reported, by the
warning that owns that subject. The entry:
[pecan]{.index entry="Pecan!Quince!Rowan"}. The target:
[sumac]{.index entry="Sumac" see="!Pecan!Quince!Rowan"}.
